items.review_rationale: Read the full pullback universal property for two arrows into S, including commutativity of fp and gq and uniqueness of a mediating arrow for every compatible pair into X and Y.

references.phrase: commuting cone to arrows X→S and Y→S
references.context: Category theory: compatible pair of arrows P→X and P→Y with equal composites to S
Category theory: universal factorization of any compatible pair of arrows to X and Y

references.disposition: These are equalities between composites in the category, not new conditions of invertibility.

items.review_rationale: Reviewed both union-of-open-subsets and greatest-open-subset formulations of the interior of A in an ambient space X; the interior depends on the topology of X.

references.phrase: open subsets of X contained in A
references.context: Topology: open subsets of the ambient topology lying within a specified subset

references.phrase: union of all such open subsets
references.disposition: The union itself is open by the topology axioms, and equals the greatest open subset contained in A.

items.review_rationale: Read both nested operations implicit in the nowhere-dense criterion: closure taken first inside X, then interior of that closure in X. This is stronger than A merely having empty interior.

references.phrase: subset A of topological space X

references.disposition: The empty-interior condition applies to the closure, not just A; no Baire-space assumption is present.

items.review_rationale: Examined geometric regularity after every finite field extension K/k, with Noetherian base algebra and its tensor extension, separately from the stated all-extension equivalence under the Stacks hypotheses. Did not equate regularity with geometric reducedness.

references.context: Commutative algebra: commutative algebra over field k via ring homomorphism
Commutative algebra: tensor-extended ring R⊗_k K with induced algebra multiplication

references.phrase: equivalent all-field-extension test under specified hypotheses
references.disposition: The all-extensions equivalence is conditioned on the indicated theorem's hypotheses, which are not silently dropped.
